page.layout: One page of text in a single column. Running head at the top with the page number 227 at top right. Below the text, an italic prayer in two indented paragraphs. Signature "L 6" at the foot, left. No marginal notes.

main_text.p: lud Publicæ Salutis Centrum, Leges, in quas omnes utinam Partes tandem definant.
Quod quidem erit multo facilius, cùm jam penitus perspectum habuerint, quàm sit multo fœlicius notis Legibus parere, quàm diversis hominum voluntatibus quantumvis blanda pollicentium.

Hæc enim Vulgi studia qui res novas fere & illicitas profequuntur, velut motus violenti statim languent, & in contumacem fere definunt morositatem; verso etiam nonnunquam in Illos impetu qui in has Illos furias perpulerunt.

Quod ad Exercitum spectat (eo forte excusatiorem quod Militari more in rem suam agant Stipendia & Indemnitatem postulantes) necessarium sane duco Paci publicæ, ut his quamprimum (quoad fas est) satis fiat. Horum enim ut ratio habeatur inprimis cupio, qui utcunque in adversa mihi acie steterint, ob fortitudinem tamen & in deposcendis periculis audaciam eoufq; sunt æstimandi, ut vehementer exoptem mihi nunquam tales defuturos, qui Me, Leges & Regna in ejusmodi Pace tueantur, cujus ipsi non minùs quam alii fructus sentiant.

p.i: Tu vero Domine qui in Sacrosancta Trinitate es perfecta Unitas, intuere illos pro tua Miseri-cordia, quos in Justitia tua divisisti.
Libera Me à contradictionibus Populi, & fac

page.notes: The mark at the lower right, beside the signature, is a small squiggle that may be a catchword or a printer's mark; I could not read it and have left it out. The stain marks along the left edge and the blotch at the lower right are not print. The running head is set partly in Greek letters; I have copied it as far as I could read it, and "BASIAIKH" may need checking against the scan. The prayer at the foot is set in italic, so I have marked it with <i>.
